title: The Panama Canal Just Passed The Suez
hook: The Suez lost half its ships.
source: Suez Canal Authority annual navigation reports, calendar-year vessel transits: 2019 18,880; 2020 18,830; 2021 20,694; 2022 23,851; 2023 26,434 (all-time record); 2024 13,213 (a ~50% collapse after Houthi attacks on Red Sea shipping pushed carriers around the Cape of Good Hope); 2025 12,758. Panama Canal Authority (ACP) fiscal-year transits of deep-draft and small commercial vessels: FY2019 ~13,785; FY2020 ~13,369; FY2021 13,342; FY2022 ~14,239; FY2023 ~14,080; FY2024 11,240 (Gatun Lake drought forced booking-slot cuts); FY2025 ~13,400 (ACP reported over 13,400 transits, +19.3% year over year). The two series use different accounting years (Suez calendar, Panama Oct-Sep fiscal) and Panama's FY2019/FY2020 figures are rounded; the crossover in 2025 is the point and it is real in both datasets. Context: attacks on commercial vessels in the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden are continuing, with Yemen's Mokha port suspending operations after strikes reported by Reuters in mid-August 2026.
